classification.difficultyReason: Transform a linear combination of sine and cosine, then solve on a restricted degree domain.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Transform the LHS into the form $C\sin(x+\alpha)$, where $C>0$ and $0^\circ\le\alpha<360^\circ$.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}C\sin(x+\alpha)&=C\sin x\cos\alpha+C\cos x\sin\alpha\\C\cos\alpha&=\sqrt5\\C\sin\alpha&=2\\C^2\cos^2\alpha+C^2\sin^2\alpha&=5+4\\C^2&=9\\C&=3\\\tan\alpha&=\frac{2}{\sqrt5}\\\alpha&=\tan^{-1}\frac{2}{\sqrt5}\approx41^\circ49'\end{align*}$$
Both coefficients are positive, so $\alpha$ is in quadrant I.
$$\sqrt5\sin x+2\cos x=3\sin\left(x+\tan^{-1}\frac{2}{\sqrt5}\right).$$

children.label: b
children.prompt: Find, correct to the nearest minute where necessary, the solutions of the equation, for $0^\circ\le x\le360^\circ$.

answer.worked:
Using $\alpha=\tan^{-1}(\frac{2}{\sqrt5})$ without rounding,
$$\begin{align*}3\sin(x+\alpha)&=-2\\\sin(x+\alpha)&=-\frac23\end{align*}$$
Since $\sin\alpha=\frac{2}{3}$ and $\alpha$ is acute, the angles in $\alpha\le x+\alpha\le360^\circ+\alpha$ are
$$\begin{align*}x+\alpha&=180^\circ+\alpha\quad\text{or}\quad360^\circ-\alpha\\x&=180^\circ\quad\text{or}\quad360^\circ-2\alpha\\x&=180^\circ\quad\text{or}\quad276^\circ23'\quad\text{(nearest minute).}\end{align*}$$
